documents.title: DXF Group Codes in Numerical Order Reference
documents.relevant_rule: Group 1005 is an entity handle in extended data, encoded as a hexadecimal string of up to 16 digits.

documents.title: Persistent Inter-Object Reference Handles (DXF)
documents.relevant_rule: XDATA group 1005 handles behave as soft pointers and translate when referenced objects are copied or inserted.

proof.source: Generated physical XDATA, imported typed values, five unique source handles, captured LINE roles, and model-space owner bindings agree. The five target LINEs are independently matched by their distinct start-X values.
proof.output: Across all four ASCII/binary source-output pairs, staged physical output checks exact ordered XDATA and remapped handles. Fresh typed readback verifies all five references point to their corresponding emitted model-space LINE and owner.
proof.failure_retry: For all four encoding pairs, removal of the fifth target refuses atomically and preserves a destination sentinel; restoring its saved list position succeeds on the same adapter. A late mutation of the fifth target handle also refuses with destination preservation; restoring the source handle succeeds on the same adapter and rechecks output/readback.

validation.asan: NOT_RUN; this slice expands runtime-generated tests and does not change production ownership, allocation, lifetime or parser behavior.

limits: This qualifies five ordered code-1005 references to distinct model-space LINEs in one AC1027 simple-LTYPE XDATA profile. Six-or-more references, other target types/sections, different XDATA compositions, versions and application meanings remain unqualified.
This is selected transport and identity evidence only. It does not establish recursive document closure, native MLINE rendering or broader format support.
